episode_title: The Interesting People You Meeting: Episode 44 "Insights From a Retirement Expert"

real_qa.q: What inspired Gary Poyer to write Make Retiring Easy and how did he develop his retirement planning approach?
real_qa.r: As a certified financial planner, Gary discovered that most of his clients did not have real plans for retirement beyond saving money. He investigated how to help them by exploring the personal growth industry and found life principles he could apply to retirement planning. This led him to leave RBC, create a workshop to help people develop a vision and retirement life plan, and eventually write Make Retiring Easy, designed as a template for financial advisors to help their clients.
real_qa.requete: Gary Poyer Make Retiring Easy inspiration

real_qa.q: What is Gary Poyer's approach to helping retirement clients define their retirement vision when they don't know where to start?
real_qa.r: Gary uses a timeline exercise where clients mark their date of birth, today's date, desired retirement date, and 20 years into retirement. He then has them define their retirement vision using three to five adjectives. Once they know their vision, he works with them to identify what activities align with that vision by looking at retirement as a time of opportunity, exploring options from relaxation to starting new businesses, reinventing themselves, and deepening personal relationships.

real_qa.q: According to Gary Poyer, what is a major misconception about retirement planning that financial advisors often make?
real_qa.r: Many financial advisors tell clients not to worry about what they will do in retirement and to figure it out when they retire. Gary takes the opposite view, believing retirement brings a sense of urgency. He states clients should know exactly what they will do on their first day of retirement and what they want to accomplish in the first three to five years, because people procrastinate, years go by quickly, and lost time cannot be regained.
real_qa.requete: retirement misconception figure out after retiring

real_qa.q: What does Gary Poyer mean by saying retirement offers a world of potential and how can retirees access it?
real_qa.r: Many people don't see retirement as offering potential because they think only from their own life experiences and comfort zone. Gary encourages people to go beyond their comfort zone by reflecting on opportunities they took advantage of and those they missed. He recommends reading books, attending workshops, talking to financial advisors, and being proactive in asking people how they use their time in retirement to realize that retirement is the final frontier offering significant opportunity if people are willing to seek it out.
real_qa.requete: retirement world of potential comfort zone

real_qa.q: How does Gary Poyer use life purpose exercises to help business owners and professionals transition into retirement?
real_qa.r: Many business owners and professionals identify themselves with what they do, so when they leave their profession they face an identity loss. Gary conducts a life purpose exercise to help them understand that just because they were a lawyer or business owner for 40 years does not mean they have to remain defined by that role. Their life purpose can evolve, and they can discover a new purpose even if they haven't previously identified one, giving them direction and preventing the sense of being lost.
real_qa.requete: business owner retirement identity life purpose

real_qa.q: What is Gary Poyer's position on leaving a personal legacy versus a financial legacy in retirement?
real_qa.r: Gary believes a personal legacy is even better than a financial legacy. While many clients want to leave money for children or grandchildren, recording your own life story—whether as video, recording, or handwritten—creates a personal legacy that generations from now will read and be amazed by, similar to how people today appreciate stories of historical figures like Ben Franklin or Canadian prime ministers.
real_qa.requete: personal legacy versus financial legacy retirement

guest.bio_context: Gary graduated from the University of Saskatchewan in 1986 and began his financial services career with Canada Trust as an assistant branch manager. He worked as a financial consultant with Investors Group in Winnipeg for seven years, attaining his Certified Financial Planner designation in 2004. In 2006, he moved to Calgary to become an investment and retirement planner with RBC Wealth Management. At the end of 2013, he left the financial services industry to create Aspire Personal Achievement, Inc. and is also an author of Make Retiring Easy.
